title: How Can You Spot Fake News Talk to Others!
paragraphs: Fake news can spread very quickly online, and it is not always easy to tell what is true. However, a new study from Italy suggests that one simple way to spot fake news is to talk about it with other people.

The study was led by Diana Carbone of the University of Trieste. It was published in the journal PLOS ONE in May 2026. It involved 111 college students, with an average age of about 21, who were put into groups of three.

The students read four news stories. Two were true, and two were fake. One fake story claimed that COVID-19 vaccines contain a chemical linked to cancer. One true story was about a Canadian company that made a chocolate spread containing cannabis. The students rated how true each story was before and after an activity. For two stories, they thought about them alone. For the other two, they talked about them with their group online for up to six minutes.

The results showed that talking in a group helped students recognize fake news. However, thinking about the stories alone did not help. Interestingly, the discussions did not change how students judged the true stories.
The effect also seemed to last. After students discussed one fake story in a group, they were better at spotting a different fake story on their own.

However, the people in the group mattered. When students talked with partners who were good at spotting fake news, about 73% of them improved. But when their partners were less accurate, about 36% got worse. Interestingly, students who already knew each other did not improve more than other students.
The study had some limitations. It was small, it only used four news stories and all the participants were college students. Most of them were women. So, more research is needed.
